title: Grade 8 Science — Tue, May 26
description: Microorganisms — Day 2 of 5: Useful microorganisms — food, medicine, agriculture
subject: science

questions.question: Yeast is used to make bread 'rise' because it:
options: Produces oxygen that inflates the bread
Carries out fermentation producing CO₂ gas, which makes dough puff up
Produces water vapour inside the bread
Breaks down gluten to create air pockets
questions.explanation: Yeast ferments sugar in dough: sugar → CO₂ + alcohol. CO₂ bubbles make dough rise. When baked, alcohol evaporates. This is why bread has a spongy texture.

questions.question: Curd (yogurt) is made from milk using:
questions.explanation: Lactobacillus bacteria ferment lactose (milk sugar) into lactic acid. This acidifies milk and causes proteins to coagulate = curd. Adding a little curd (starter) provides the bacteria.

questions.question: Penicillin — the first antibiotic — was discovered from:
questions.explanation: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin in 1928 from Penicillium notatum mould. He noticed it killed bacteria growing on a petri dish. This revolutionised medicine — antibiotics save millions of lives.

questions.question: Antibiotics work by:
options: Killing or stopping growth of BACTERIA (not viruses)
questions.explanation: Antibiotics target bacterial structures (cell wall, ribosomes). They do NOT work against viruses. Taking antibiotics for viral infections (cold, flu) is wrong and causes antibiotic resistance.

questions.question: Vaccines work by:
options: Introducing weakened/dead pathogens to train the immune system
Replacing damaged cells with healthy ones
questions.explanation: Vaccines introduce dead or weakened pathogens (or their proteins). The immune system produces antibodies. Future infection: immune system 'remembers' and quickly destroys the pathogen. Edward Jenner made the first vaccine (smallpox, 1796).

questions.question: Rhizobium bacteria are important in agriculture because they:
options: Decompose dead organic matter in soil
Fix atmospheric nitrogen into a form plants can use (live in root nodules of legumes)
Produce CO₂ that plants use for photosynthesis
questions.explanation: Rhizobium lives in root nodules of leguminous plants (peas, beans, clover). It converts N₂ gas from air into ammonia/nitrates that plants absorb. This is biological nitrogen fixation — natural fertiliser!

questions.question: Decomposers like fungi and bacteria play what role in the ecosystem?
options: They compete with plants for sunlight
They break down dead organisms and recycle nutrients back into the soil
They are only harmful to the environment
questions.explanation: Decomposers break down dead organic matter → release nutrients (N, P, K) back into soil → plants absorb them. Without decomposers, dead organisms would pile up and nutrients would be locked away forever.

questions.question: Which microorganism is used to make beer, wine, and alcohol?
questions.explanation: Yeast carries out anaerobic fermentation: glucose → ethanol (alcohol) + CO₂. Used for beer (from barley), wine (from grapes), spirits. Also used in bread making.

questions.question: Biofertilisers are:
options: Living microorganisms that improve soil fertility naturally
questions.explanation: Biofertilisers contain living microorganisms (Rhizobium, Azotobacter, mycorrhizal fungi) that improve soil nutrients naturally. Cheaper, eco-friendly alternative to chemical fertilisers.

questions.question: Why is curd (with Lactobacillus) considered probiotic?
options: It kills all bacteria in the gut
It introduces beneficial live bacteria that improve gut health and digestion
It is a type of antibiotic
questions.explanation: Probiotics = live beneficial bacteria that improve gut microbiome. Lactobacillus in curd aids digestion, boosts immunity, and prevents harmful bacteria from colonising the gut.

questions.question: Fermentation is defined as:
options: Oxygen-requiring breakdown of glucose to CO₂ and water
Breakdown of organic compounds by microorganisms WITHOUT oxygen (anaerobic process)
The process of photosynthesis in algae
questions.explanation: Fermentation = anaerobic breakdown of carbohydrates by microorganisms. Products: alcohol + CO₂ (yeast) OR lactic acid (bacteria). Used in food production for thousands of years.

questions.question: Insulin (for diabetes treatment) is now produced using:
options: Genetically modified bacteria (E. coli) that produce human insulin
questions.explanation: Human insulin gene is inserted into E. coli bacteria. The bacteria then produce human insulin in huge quantities. This is recombinant DNA technology — safer, cheaper, no animal-derived insulin needed.

questions.question: Sewage treatment plants use microorganisms to:
options: Add chemicals to kill all bacteria in water
Decompose organic waste in sewage, making water safe for environment
Convert sewage into drinking water directly
questions.explanation: Aerobic bacteria decompose organic matter in sewage. Anaerobic bacteria produce biogas. The treated water is then safe to release or be further treated for use. Microorganisms are essential to waste management.

questions.question: Biogas is produced by:
options: Anaerobic decomposition of organic matter by methane-producing bacteria (methanogens)
questions.explanation: Methanogenic bacteria decompose organic waste (cattle dung, food waste) without oxygen → produce biogas (mainly methane + CO₂). Biogas is used as cooking fuel in rural India.

questions.question: Match the microorganism to its use: Lactobacillus / Yeast / Rhizobium / Penicillium
options: Curd / Bread & alcohol / Nitrogen fixation / Antibiotic
questions.explanation: LACTOBACILLUS→curd. YEAST→bread & alcohol. RHIZOBIUM→nitrogen fixation (root nodules of legumes). PENICILLIUM→penicillin antibiotic. Four key useful microorganisms.
